description: Built by Fiat in 1960, Werknummer 0060. On loan from the Militärhistorisches Museum Dresden. Museum website, 2026.

Construction number 1734. Displayed in the markings JB-110 of Jagdgeschwader 72 at Leck; previously displayed at Oldenburg and then Militärhistorisches Museum Dresden, on loan to Rothenburg since April 2007.
Ex-Bundesluftwaffe target tug, airframe number 338-06, also flown as D-9550. On loan from the Militärhistorisches Museum Dresden, where it was displayed until autumn 2005.
Spanish-built Dornier Do 27, serial U9-36, completed by CASA in Seville on 28 September 1961 and flown by the Ejercito del Aire; written off 1992 and donated to the museum in December 2010.
Airframe number 7311. On loan from the Luftwaffenmuseum Berlin-Gatow since 2006.
Delivered to the NVA in September 1977, airframe number 75051378; served with JG-8 at Marxwalde (Neuhardenberg) and flew 1126 hours.
Ex-NVA MiG-21F-13 displayed with tactical number 623; previously used by the Offiziershochschule/AFS.
Delivered to the NVA August 1969, airframe number 0508; flew 1629 hours and served last with TAFS-47 at Preschen.
Ex-NVA MiG-21MF, airframe number 96002170.
Ex-NVA MiG-21SPS-K, airframe number 7215.
Ex-NVA two-seat MiG-21U-600, airframe number 4818.
Ex-NVA two-seat MiG-21U recorded at Rothenburg in the NVA MiG-21 fate register at mig-21.de; the museum website details only the U-600 296, so this airframe may be stored rather than displayed.
Ex-NVA two-seat MiG-21US, airframe number 5685134 of the 34th production series.
Taken on NVA charge June 1966, airframe number 692061; flew with JAG-11/JAG-25 at Bautzen until 1980, then used as a strafing target at Rothenburg and recovered as the museum's founding exhibit.
Airframe number 692054. Stood for years in Dresden; transferred to Rothenburg in spring 2007 as a loan from the Militärhistorisches Museum.
Ex-NVA L-39, airframe number ZD-731005.
Czechoslovak-built MiG-15UTI, serial 722651, built at Aero Prag-Vysocany in 1957 and delivered to the DDR in February 1958 for JAG-25 at Bautzen.
Ex-NVA MiG-17F, airframe number 1C06-30.
Ex-NVA MiG-19PM, airframe number 65929; restored by the museum from 2007.
Ex-NVA MiG-23BN, airframe number 393211085.
Airframe number 26817; taken on charge April 1985 with Marinefliegergeschwader 28 at Laage and flew 576 hours before the Bundeswehr withdrew the type.

Nose/cockpit section only, taken from an A319 dismantled at Rothenburg by Elbe Flugzeugwerke Dresden between 2020 and 2022; acquired by the museum as a walk-in exhibit. Registration of the donor airframe not published.
